sections.h2: Where is Horn Lake and what is it like to sell a house there?
sections.html:
Horn Lake is a DeSoto County city on the Tennessee line, just south of Memphis. U.S. 51 forms much of its eastern border and leads 15 miles north to downtown Memphis and 9 miles south to Hernando, the county seat. Interstate 55 passes just east of the city with access from Exits 287, 289 and 901, and the city is bordered by Southaven to the east and southeast.

The city covers 16.3 square miles, nearly all of it land. Its main east-west road is Goodman Road, which is also Mississippi Highways 301 and 302. The nearest airport is Memphis International, about seven miles from the center of town.

Memphis is the closest big city, so a Horn Lake seller is often dealing with a market that spans a state line. Ask your title company and insurer whether they work in Mississippi, and expect Mississippi rules, not Tennessee ones, to govern your deed, your taxes and your disclosure form.

sections.h2: How did Horn Lake grow from a railroad stop to a suburb?
sections.html:
Horn Lake was a rural crossing for most of its history and became a suburb only in the second half of the twentieth century. The name comes from an oxbow lake about three miles west, a former channel of the Mississippi River shaped like a cow horn. The Mississippi and Tennessee Railroad, later the Illinois Central, reached the community in 1856, and Horn Lake Academy opened in 1867.

Two attempts at incorporation failed. The first, in 1850, did not take, and an 1871 charter was revoked after the 1890 census found only 99 residents. Interstate 55 opened in 1964, and in 1970 First Mississippi Corporation began developing about 960 acres as DeSoto Village. The city incorporated permanently in 1973.

The census numbers tell the rest. The population was 2,170 in 1970, then 14,099 in 2000, 26,066 in 2010 and 26,736 in 2020. Growth since 2010 has been slow, and most of the city's building boom came after 1970.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about households in Horn Lake?
sections.html:
The 2024 American Community Survey estimated 10,072 households in Horn Lake with an average of 2.64 persons per household. The city has 10,987 housing units, a median household income of $53,311, and a median age of 33.5 years. About 19.0 percent of residents live at or below the poverty line.

The gap between 10,987 housing units and 10,072 households may reflect vacant homes, including homes for sale, rentals and properties between occupants. If you own one that is empty, insurance, utilities and security are costs you carry every month.

sections.h2: Who works in Horn Lake, and which schools serve it?
sections.html:
Horn Lake has a mix of industry and institutions rather than one dominant employer. A Newly Weds Foods plant makes food coatings and seasonings here, and the American Contract Bridge League keeps its headquarters, museum and Hall of Fame in the city. Elvis Presley's 154.5 acre ranch, owned during the last decade of his life, is also in Horn Lake.

Public schools belong to the DeSoto County School District. The city's schools include Horn Lake High School, Horn Lake Middle School, Horn Lake Intermediate School, Horn Lake Elementary School and Shadow Oaks Elementary School. The DeSoto County Career and Technology Center West is also in the area.

Public transit options are limited. Wikipedia notes there is no fixed-route transit within DeSoto County, and the Delta Rides region provides service to employment centers and medical facilities, while Memphis Area Transit Authority, Amtrak and Greyhound serve nearby Memphis. A seller without a car may find a single closing appointment easier than repeated showings.

sections.h2: What city rules matter when you sell in Horn Lake?
sections.html:
The Planning and Development Department reviews plans, approves permits and issues business licenses, and Code Enforcement is at 3101 Goodman Road West. Permits are handled through an online portal. Code Enforcement takes reports at codeviolations@hornlake.org, by direct line at 662-342-3507, and through the city's 311 request page.

The city also has a rental housing code. A draft ordinance posted on the city's site states that its intent is to set base standards for rental housing so as to prevent or correct slum and blighted conditions. If you rent out your Horn Lake house, ask the city whether the final rule applies to you before you sell or transfer it.

  • Check for open permits on any work done by a prior owner or contractor.
  • Ask Code Enforcement whether any complaint is open on your address.
  • Confirm utility accounts, since water and sanitation bills are paid to the city.

The city's ordinances are published through Municode, and resolving any open items before closing keeps surprises off the settlement statement.

sections.h2: How do DeSoto County property taxes and homestead filing work?
sections.html:
Property taxes in Mississippi are due by February 1 for the preceding assessment, and DeSoto County takes payments at tax collector offices in Hernando, Olive Branch and Horn Lake, as well as by mail and online. The Mississippi Department of Revenue sets the assessment ratios: 10 percent of true value for a single-family, owner-occupied home and 15 percent for other real property.

The DeSoto County Tax Assessor, Jeff Fitch, helps homeowners with homestead exemption applications from January 1 through April 1. The county says it will start accepting applications at 8:00 AM on January 4, 2027 with a filing deadline of 5:00 PM on April 1, 2027, and first-time applicants file at 365 Losher Street, Suite 100 in Hernando.

sections.h2: What are your options for a fast sale in Horn Lake?
sections.html:
You can list the house, sell privately, or take a cash offer, and the trade is speed and certainty against price. Mississippi law, in Sections 89-1-501 through 89-1-523 of the Mississippi Code, requires a covered seller to deliver a written property condition disclosure statement to the buyer before title transfers.

A cash buyer can purchase a Horn Lake house as is, which suits inherited homes, houses with deferred repairs, and rentals with tenant issues. The Chancery Clerk in DeSoto County records the deed after closing.

Get more than one number before you decide. An honest offer will show how the buyer reached it, and you should expect to compare it with what a listing nets after commissions, repairs and carrying costs. We make no promise about price, and you can say no.

faqs.a: Horn Lake is a city in DeSoto County in the northwest corner of Mississippi, bordering Southaven and sitting about 15 miles south of downtown Memphis along U.S. 51.

faqs.q: When does DeSoto County accept homestead exemption applications?
faqs.a: The county says applications open at 8:00 AM on January 4, 2027 and close at 5:00 PM on April 1, 2027. First-time filers apply at the Tax Assessor's Office at 365 Losher Street, Suite 100, Hernando.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a code complaint in Horn Lake?
faqs.a: Call the Code Enforcement direct line at 662-342-3507 or email codeviolations@hornlake.org. The office is at 3101 Goodman Road West.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Horn Lake?
faqs.a: The DeSoto County School District serves Horn Lake. Its local campuses include Horn Lake High School, Horn Lake Middle School and Horn Lake Elementary School.

faqs.q: Where can I pay DeSoto County property taxes in Horn Lake?
faqs.a: The county lists tax collector offices in Hernando, Olive Branch and Horn Lake, and also accepts payment by mail and online. Taxes are due by February 1 under state law.

faqs.q: Do I have to give buyers a disclosure statement in Mississippi?
faqs.a: Covered sellers must deliver a written property condition disclosure statement to the buyer as soon as practicable before title transfers, under Sections 89-1-501 through 89-1-523. Check with your agent or attorney about exemptions.
